extraction_metadata.notes: Extracted from a LinkedIn post by Aloush Ali Gharib (Bioinformatics Research Scholar) sharing the published Wiley open-access article. The post embeds a custom graphical abstract spanning computational (molecular docking + 200 ns MD) and in vitro (SH-SY5Y cellular) findings.

title: Neuroprotective Effect of Magnoflorine Through Inhibition of Caspase-3-Mediated Neuronal Apoptosis: In Silico to In Vitro Validation
subtitle_or_tagline: From computer → molecules → proteins → cells: a docking-prediction validated in neuronal culture.
topic: Magnoflorine (a plant alkaloid) is computationally predicted by molecular docking + 200 ns molecular dynamics to bind Caspase-3, then validated in vitro on differentiated SH-SY5Y cells where it rescues viability, lowers LDH release, suppresses apoptosis, and reduces Caspase-3 expression elevated by kainic acid.

components.name: Molecular Docking
components.role: Snap-shot prediction of Magnoflorine ↔ Caspase-3 binding pose and affinity.

components.name: 200 ns Molecular Dynamics
components.role: Temporal refinement of the docking pose — converts the static snapshot into a stability trajectory (RMSD / fluctuation over time).

components.name: SH-SY5Y Cellular Assay Panel
components.role: In vitro validation on differentiated dopaminergic-like neurons: MTT viability, LDH damage, Annexin-V apoptosis flow cytometry, Caspase-3 immunofluorescence.

architecture.data_flow: In silico: Magnoflorine structure → Docking vs Caspase-3 → 200 ns MD trajectory → predicted neuroprotective hypothesis. In vitro: SH-SY5Y + Kainic acid ± Magnoflorine → MTT/LDH/Annexin-V/Caspase-3 panels → cellular confirmation.

workflow_steps: Step 1 - Pose the question: does Magnoflorine protect neurons, and is Caspase-3 the mechanism?
Step 2 - In silico: molecular docking of Magnoflorine into the Caspase-3 active site.
Step 3 - In silico: 200 ns MD simulation to track complex stability over time (RMSD, fluctuation).
Step 4 - In vitro: differentiate SH-SY5Y cells, induce damage with kainic acid, treat with Magnoflorine.
Step 5 - In vitro: read out MTT viability, LDH release, Annexin-V apoptosis, Caspase-3 expression.
Step 6 - Connect the chain: molecular interaction → MD stability → viability → apoptosis → Caspase-3.
key_claims: Magnoflorine docked into Caspase-3 and formed a stable complex across 200 ns of MD.
Trajectory stability is non-stationary: kainic-acid complex was more stable early, Magnoflorine complex more stable late.
Magnoflorine rescued SH-SY5Y viability from 46.9% (KA) to 85.2% (KA + Magnoflorine).
LDH release fell from 286.2% (KA) to 132.9% (KA + Magnoflorine).
Early apoptosis fell from 29.8% to 13.4%; late apoptosis from 34.9% to 3.1%.
Kainic acid raised Caspase-3 expression; Magnoflorine reduced that elevation.
Computational prediction → biological hypothesis → experimental validation is the demonstrated pipeline.
caveats_or_warnings: Docking + 200 ns MD is a hypothesis generator, not proof of binding or mechanism.
SH-SY5Y is a cell line, not primary tissue — in vivo validation is still required.
Findings support a potential neuroprotective role and Caspase-3 pathway involvement; they do NOT establish Magnoflorine as a treatment.
Author explicitly notes in vivo work is the next required step before any translational claim.
